paper.title: A/B/n Testing with Control in the Presence of Subpopulations

settings.name_in_paper: ABC-S problem (active, proportional and agnostic modes)
unmapped: Goal: identify the set of all arms whose weighted mean sum_i beta_i mu_{a,i} exceeds that of an unknown control arm 0
Population stratified into J subpopulations; arm-subpopulation pairs have their own exponential-family distributions
Modes of interaction: active (learner picks subpopulation), proportional (subpopulation I_t ~ alpha observed before arm choice), agnostic (I_t observed after arm choice)
Learner knows J, importance vector beta and subpopulation frequencies alpha
Safely calibrated policies: anytime risk assessment hat delta_t with P(exists t: wrong answer and hat delta_t <= delta) <= delta
settings.definition_quote: For $\vbeta \in \mathbb{R}^J$ we define the ABC-S problem as the correct identification of the set $\mathcal{S}_{\vbeta}(\vmu) \df \{a \in [K] : \sum_{i=1}^J \beta_i \mu_{a,i} > \sum_{i=1}^J \beta_i \mu_{0,i}\}$.

unmapped: Goal: identify all arms better than an unknown control arm in weighted mean
Subpopulation is not observed; rewards are mixtures sum_i alpha_i nu_{a,i} of exponential-family distributions
Safely calibrated policies with anytime risk assessment
settings.definition_quote: In the oblivious mode, the subpopulations can not be observed by the learner. In this case, we have ... $X_t | A_t = a \sim \sum_{i=1}^J \alpha_i \nu_{a,i}$.

symbols.T_star_ABC: characteristic time of the ABC-S problem for the given mode: T*(mu)^{-1} = sup_{w in C} inf_{lambda in Alt_beta(mu)} sum_{a,i} w_{a,i} d(mu_{a,i}, lambda_{a,i}), C the mode's sampling-constraint set

conditions: mu in L (no arm has the same weighted mean as the control)

source.label: th:generic_sample_comp
source.quote: Let $\delta \in (0,1)$ and $\vbeta \in \mathbb{R}^J$. For any strategy satisfying Equation~\ref{eq:p-value} and any $\vmu \in\mathcal{L}$, the expected number of rounds for the ABC-S problem for the agnostic, proportional and active mode satisfies: $\mathbb{E}_\vmu[\tau_{\delta}] \geq T^\star(\vmu) \,\textnormal{kl}(\delta, 1- \delta)$ and $\liminf_{\delta \to 0} \frac{\mathbb{E}_\vmu[\tau_\delta]}{\ln(1/\delta)} \geq T^\star(\vmu)$

results.notes: T* depends on mode via constraint set C (ordering T_active <= T_prop <= T_agnostic). Proposition charsingle restates the same bound for J=1 with T* = sup_w min_b d_mid; Proposition proposition_others_weights gives closed-form T* for Gaussian K=1 in each mode.

symbols.T_star_ABC: characteristic time of the ABC-S problem for the given mode (sup over C of inf over alternatives of weighted divergence, inverted)

results.notes: Asymptotic form of the same theorem.

symbols.T_star_obl: oblivious characteristic time: inverse of sup_{w in Sigma_{K+1}} inf_{nu' in Alt} sum_a w_a KL(sum_i alpha_i nu_{a,i}, sum_i alpha_i nu'_{a,i}); satisfies T_star_obl >= T_agnostic

conditions: oblivious strategy satisfying Equation eq:p-value (safely calibrated)

source.label: prop:sample_comp_oblivious
source.quote: Let $\delta \in (0,1)$ and $\vbeta \in \mathbb{R}^J$. For any \textit{oblivious} strategy satisfying Equation~\ref{eq:p-value} and any $\vmu \in \mathcal{L}$, the characteristic time satisfies $\mathbb{E}_\vmu[\tau_{\delta}] \geq T_{\textnormal{oblivious}}^\star(\vmu) \,\textnormal{kl}(\delta, 1- \delta)$ ... Furthermore, $T_{\textnormal{oblivious}}^\star(\vmu) \geq T_{\textnormal{agnostic}}^\star(\vmu)$.

conditions: oblivious strategy satisfying Equation eq:p-value (safely calibrated)

symbols.T_star_ABC: characteristic time of the ABC-S problem for the given mode

tuning: C-tracking with forced exploration (proof); threshold beta(t,delta) from Kaufmann & Koolen Prop. 23 / ln(t^2/delta)+O(1)

source.label: thm:asym.opt
source.quote: For every mode, Subpopulation Track-and-Stop is safely calibrated (Equation~\ref{eq:p-value}). Moreover, Subpopulation Track-and-Stop is asymptotically optimal and matches the lower bound from Theorem~\ref{th:generic_sample_comp}, in the sense that for every bandit $\vmu \in \mathcal L$, $\lim_{\delta \to 0} \frac{\mathbb{E}[\tau_\delta]}{\ln(1/\delta)} = T^\star(\vmu)$.

results.notes: Limit equals T*; recorded as limsup upper bound. Proof relies on Degenne & Koolen 2019; per-iteration runtime O(K J^2). 'Every mode' refers to active/proportional/agnostic for which the algorithm is defined.
